metadata.task_prompt: The full JSON procurement workbook is stored in the Python variable context. Load it with json.loads(context). Select exactly one quote for each of the five SKUs A-E. Quotes are indivisible lots. Each selected quote must supply at least the SKU demand and at most demand+2 units, must arrive on or before that SKU's deadline, and must have quality approved. Across all selected quotes, use at least three vendors, keep total carbon <= carbon_cap, and keep each vendor's total selected units <= unit_cap. If a quote has needs_same_vendor_sku, the quote selected for that other SKU must come from the same vendor. For each vendor, compute gross=sum(units*unit_cents). If that vendor's selected units >= tier_units, apply its tier_bps discount to the entire gross; round the vendor's merchandise total to cents, with exact halves rounded up. Add shipping_cents unless the PRE-DISCOUNT gross >= free_shipping_gross. Subtract rebate_cents only if at least two different SKUs are selected from that vendor AND the POST-DISCOUNT merchandise total >= rebate_merchandise_min. All thresholds are inclusive. Total cost is the sum over all vendors used. Find the globally minimum total cost in cents, not the result of a greedy per-SKU choice. Return only that integer using print(FINAL(str(answer))) or submit_answer. All values and rules are fictional for this experiment. No orders will be placed.
